flags: Dropped the current hardwood-canopy claim: the cached MDOT PDF is only a Wayback navigation stub. The highway article supports forest and woodland but does not identify hardwoods or canopy.

The cached biography uses Grand River Band of Ottawa Nation; material also uses Odawa/Odawas. No tribal source is cached to resolve preferred terminology. The story follows the biography’s name and omits detailed treaty and battle accounts.

Noahquageshik’s dates conflict within the cached biography (1755–1855 or 1770–1840); no lifespan dates are used. The inherited tomahawk and hat claim is supported there but omitted for focus and lack of stronger sourcing.
The highway’s 1998 transfer to state control and its 1999 number assignment are separate from byway designation. The cache does not establish a byway designation date or drive time.
Bradley remains short because the cache provides only a brief founding account and road geography. Its current photo coordinate is retained despite differing from material’s strip coordinate.

Gun Lake is a separate excursion: the cache places M-179 north of it but does not establish a lake view from the highway. Its river scene value is retained because the permitted vocabulary has no lake category.
